title: Shard-aware stochastic prefetch scheduler + adaptive kernel routing to reduce embedding p95
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce p95/p99 tail for the embeddings endpoint at 95% and 99% across mixed-tenant traffic without degrading average throughput or increasing cost more than 6%.

Background: Recent postmortem of embed-tail incidents shows that a large fraction of p95 spikes come from two correlated sources: (1) cold shard page faults / KV cache misses when tenants send long contexts or sparse corpus lookups, and (2) suboptimal kernel selection for short vs. long sequences causing kernel scheduling thrash and occasional context preemption. Previous tickets focused on microbatching heuristics and coarse kernel hints; this ticket experiments with an integrated approach that combines stochastic, shard-aware prefetching with an adaptive kernel routing policy driven by a lightweight latency model.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Implement a shard-aware stochastic prefetch scheduler that uses recent shard-hit rates and tenant soft-deadlines to opportunistically prefetch hot KV ranges into GPU memory ahead of request servicing.
- Add a per-request kernel-latency predictor (simple regression + lookup table) that chooses between fast-quantized kernels or high-throughput kernels based on expected latencies for the current sequence length and temperature.
- End-to-end engineering measurable criteria: p95 reduced by >= 18% and p99 reduced by >= 12% on benchmark traffic (mixed real tenant traces) while increasing unit GPU token cost by <= 6%.
- No regressions on average throughput and no increase in tail due to prefetch flooding (safety limits required).

Non-goals: large model architecture changes, changing model quantization formats globally, or replacing the batching runtime.

Technical approach:
1) Prefetch scheduler
   - Maintain lightweight per-shard EWMA of hit-rate and recent inter-arrival times.
   - Use a stochastic prefetch decision: if P(prefetch) = f(hit_rate, ai, tenant_deadline_headroom) > threshold, enqueue prefetch for top-k hot keys for that shard.
   - Prefetch backpressure: global concurrent prefetch window (configurable per-pool) with token-based admission to avoid IO storms.
   - Eviction hinting: prefetches annotate items with short TTL and a conservative residency hint to avoid blowing GPU memory.

2) Kernel routing
   - Train a small on-node latency table: (model, seq_len_bucket, kernel_variant) -> quantile latency estimates (p50,p95).
   - At request enqueue time, consult the table plus current batch size to pick kernel_variant that minimizes expected latency subject to throughput SLO.
   - Add runtime override rules for tenants with explicit SLA to prefer lower p95 kernels even if cost heavier.

3) Observability and safety
   - Add new metrics: prefetch_rate_per_shard, prefetch_hit_rate, prefetch_eviction_rate, kernel_switch_count, predicted_vs_actual_latency.
   - Implement a canary rollout that enables prefetching and model-driven kernel routing for 2% of production traffic with aggressive sampling and an automatic rollback trigger based on p95 worsened by >5%.

Implementation plan:
- Spike (1 week): prototype prefetch policy in local dev runtime using captured traces; implement kernel latency table generator from recent perf data.
- Integrate (2 weeks): add admission control and eviction hints; wire the latency table into the dispatch path.
- Canary (1 week): deploy on staging and 2% production, compare with baseline over rolling 48h windows.
- Rollout & tuning (2 weeks): tune thresholds, backpressure windows, and tenant overrides.

Notes on safety trade-offs:
- Aggressive prefetching reduces request latency but risks memory starvation; we enforce a global prefetch token pool and per-tenant budgets.
- Kernel routing may increase average cost if we favor low-latency kernels; we will gate this with tenant-level override flags and cost-budget guards.

Deliverables:
- Runtime changes + integration tests
- Kernel latency table generator script and trainer job
- Dashboards for the new metrics
- Canary playbook and rollback automation
- Short PRD + perf writeup with benchmark results and cost analysis
